claims.title: kubectl rollout restart runs unconditionally, defeating the purpose of masking it to only-when-needed secret changes
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**kubectl rollout restart runs unconditionally, defeating the purpose of masking it to only-when-needed secret changes**

The new `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ai-listings` runs on every invocation of the script regardless of whether the Secret actually changed, which is functionally correct for ensuring new env vars are picked up, but it means every deploy now always triggers a full pod restart even when nothing changed (e.g., a no-op re-run). This isn't necessarily wrong but is worth a sanity check since it changes deploy semantics: previously a deploy with an unchanged image tag could be effectively a no-op; now it always restarts pods. If restarts are cheap and idempotent this is fine, but if the deployment has stateful init work or there are concerns about restart frequency, this should be called out.

claims.title: kubectl apply updates the Secret's stringData, but if the Deployment pod template doesn't change (e.g. TAG stays 'latest' and no other env changes), the rollout-restart added here does fire unconditionally, which does address the stale-pod-env concern. This looks resolved by the explicit `kubectl rollout restart` call before `rollout status`.

claims.title: Error from kubectl get for BROWSERLESS_TOKEN jsonpath is swallowed when the key is simply absent, but also can't distinguish RBAC failure from absence
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Error from kubectl get for BROWSERLESS_TOKEN jsonpath is swallowed when the key is simply absent, but also can't distinguish RBAC failure from absence**

The fix moves `kubectl get` outside the `if`, which correctly lets `set -e` catch a hard kubectl failure (RBAC denial, API server error) per the PR's stated intent. However, `-o jsonpath='{.data.BROWSERLESS_TOKEN}'` on a secret that doesn't have this key at all does not cause kubectl to fail — it exits 0 with empty stdout. That's the desired 'absent' path. But if the Secret `ai-listings-secret` itself doesn't exist yet (e.g. first-ever deploy before secret.yaml is applied with this key), `kubectl get secret` would fail and halt the script — but secret.yaml was just applied above so this should be fine in practice. No actionable defect here, flagging only for awareness that jsonpath on a missing key (not missing secret) silently yields empty string, which is intended behavorily correct.

claims.title: Unconditional rollout restart causes pod churn on every deploy
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Unconditional rollout restart causes pod churn on every deploy**

`kubectl rollout restart deployment/ai-listings` now runs unconditionally on every invocation of this script, even when neither the Secret nor the pod template changed (e.g. repeated deploys with the default `latest` tag and no secret value changes). This forces an unnecessary pod restart on every deploy, which is wasteful and increases risk of masking a genuinely failed rollout behind routine churn. This mirrors the already-flagged 'Rollout restart is unconditional, not Secret-change-aware' finding from a prior review round — restating here since it remains unresolved in this diff.

claims.title: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ai-listings` is now called unconditionally after every `kubectl apply`, even when neither the image tag nor the secret actually changed. This forces a pod restart (and attendant downtime/cold-start) on every no-op deploy, which is a behavior change from the prior script where rollout only happened implicitly via spec changes. Consider gating the restart on an actual diff (e.g. compare secret hash, or only restart when BROWSERLESS_TOKEN removal/STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN value actually changed) rather than running it every time.

**Comment claims gateway token key lives in stealth-browser-secrets, unverifiable and could rot**

The header comment states STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN is "the stealth-browser-secrets gatewayToken in the stealth-browser namespace". This is a specific claim about an external resource (secret name, key name, namespace) that isn't verifiable from this diff and could silently drift out of sync if the stealth-browser repo renames that secret/key later, leaving a misleading comment for future maintainers.

claims.title: Module-level warnedMissingToken flag persists across invocations within the process
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Module-level warnedMissingToken flag persists across invocations within the process**

`warnedMissingToken` is a module-level mutable flag, so once a missing-token warning fires, it never fires again for the remainder of the process lifetime, even if the token is later set and then unset again (e.g. hot env reload in long-running workers, or test isolation across files sharing the module). This is a minor logging/observability gap rather than a functional bug, but worth flagging since it could mask a later real misconfiguration.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Intentional. A 423 or 429 is expected under normal pacing, but it still means this comp went unverified, so one warn line with status and URL is the right level for every non-OK answer. Per-status log levels would add branches with no behavior change, and the gateway's own request log already records the verdict (blocked, rate_limited, queue_full). The title mentions stale token-check semantics, but this line has no token check. The token check sits above it and now warns once when the token is missing (784a049f).

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Intentional. The Secret is rewritten on every deploy and pods only read it at startup, so a restart is the only way a changed token reaches them; an unconditional restart is cheap and can't be skipped by mistake.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: A failed kubectl get does stop the script: the lookup runs in its own statement under set -e, and an absent key returns an empty result with exit 0, so the two cases are distinguishable. The check now tests for the key itself (see the empty-key thread).
